chunks: Among what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Yaqṭīnī, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jābir, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
A man came to him and said to him: “A mouse fell into a large jar containing ghee or oil; what do you say about eating it?” He said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said to him: “Do not eat it.”

He said: The man then said to him: “The mouse is less significant to me than my leaving my food because of it.” He said: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said to him: “You have not treated the mouse lightly; rather, you have treated your religion lightly. Indeed, Allah has forbidden carrion from every thing.”
Because the basis in this narration is that if the mouse dies in it, then benefiting from it in any way is not permissible.

key_terms.الِانْتِفَاعُ: deriving benefit or use; stated here as impermissible in this case
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةَ: carrion; a dead animal whose presence renders the substance forbidden here
key_terms.خَابِيَةٍ: a large storage jar or vessel containing the substance
key_terms.دِينِكَ: your religion; the Imam عليه السلام frames disregard of the ruling as disrespect toward one’s religion
key_terms.زَيْتٌ: oil mentioned as one of the affected substances
key_terms.سَمْنٌ: ghee or clarified fat mentioned as one of the affected foods
key_terms.فَأْرَةٌ: a mouse whose falling into the food is the cause of the ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mouse falls and dies in ghee or oil according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that food such as ghee or oil becomes unusable when a mouse dies in it. It also teaches that dismissing such impurity is not triviality toward the animal itself, but a disregard for one’s religion and for Allah’s prohibition of carrion.
